newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to balance of payments figures for November, released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australia recorded a current account shortfall of A$1.92 billion after seasonal adjustment - six per cent higher than the revised deficit of $1.81 billion recorded in October. Page 1.

In a deal that confirms Africa as an emerging market for Australian wheat, the Australian Wheat Board had made a 60,000 tonne sale of high protein hard wheat to Sudan, which will be delivered in three shipments in January, March and April to a new flour mill in Khartoum. Page 3.

David Jones Ltd had lodged an appeal against Justice Francis Marks' decision in Cukeric & David Jones, which together with a pending Full Bench appeal decision in a case involving a former Westfield Ltd senior executive, will test the rights of dismissed executives to win potential compensation payouts of million of dollars. Page 3.

Investors are becoming frustrated with the management of David Jones Ltd and believe the group is vulnerable to a takeover bid since it lost A$78 million off its market capitalisation from last Friday. The retailer has announced a 50 per cent slump in fist-half earnings - its fourth downgrade in the past 12 months. Page 15.

With the founding head of Jewel Food Stores, Jim Fleming, retiring after more than 25 years with the company, United States food retail executive Bob Neslund will take on the top job at a time when Jewel is struggling to match last year's profit of more tan A$15 million. Page 15.

In a move designed to force Casinos Austria International Ltd to either make a substantial capital injection or clear the way for a replacement operator of the loss-making Reef Casino at Cairns, the casino's banking syndicate, led by the ANZ Banking Corp, last week withdrew a A$15 million loan facility that covered possible junket losses. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As Advance Bank shareholders learned they would not receive the A$7.30-a-share flagged at the October launch of St George's agreed takeover bid by scheme of arrangement, the proposed A$2.65 billion merger struck a major legal hurdle as well yesterday, with the New South Wales Supreme Court questioning the fairness and legality of key aspects of the deal. Page 17.

Gold prices have slumped to a fresh three-year low, with gold for February delivery plunging US$4.60 to US$3.62 an ounce on the New York Mercantile Exchange's Comex division on Friday, its lowest since October 11, 1993. The new low sparked fierce selling of local gold stocks yesterday as investors anticipated more falls for the yellow metal. Page 17.

In response to frequent claims the Australian Securities Commission has been slow in pursuing investigations and bringing miscreants to court, the ASC has formed the Rapid Action Summary Prosecution group - a rapid response unit with a charter to protect people from losing money to dubious investment schemes. Page 17.

RTZ-CRA subsidiary Comalco Ltd revealed yesterday it has ordered a review of costs across its three aluminium smelters - Bell Bay, Boyne Island and Tiwai Point - with the review expected to result in a "relatively small" number of voluntary redundancies at each plant. Page 19.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd's annual review for the year to September 30, released yesterday, shows group managing director Geoff Tomlinson has been granted a 33 per cent salary bonus following last year's successful listing of the insurance giant, taking his salary to A$1,161,794. Page 19.

As part of its ongoing assessment of non-core activities, Telstra Corp Ltd has announced plans to sell its conformance testing assets to new local company Comtest Laboratories Pty Ltd, who will undertake work previously carried out by Comtest, Telstra's customer premises equipment conformance test house. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The structure of St George's proposed A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance Bank came under intense scrutiny in the New South Wales Supreme Court yesterday, with Justice Santow concluding the session by asking Advance to consider two major changes to the structure of the deal which could remove much of the legal ambiguity of the deemed-proxy clause. Page 12.

Following the Lend Lease Corp announcement on Sunday that it was looking at continuing global expansion through the possible acquisition of Equitable Real Estate Investment Management, the United States' largest property funds manager, shares in the group rose 10 cents yesterday to A$24.55, with 460,425 shares changing hands. Page 12.

According to figures released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics, there has been an alarming slide in Australia's trade performance, led by a drop in key exports, with merchandise exports falling five per cent, or A$312 million, in the month when adjusted for seasonal factors. Page 12.

In a result which has prompted fund managers and corporate advisers to speculate about the price at which a predator would be interested in raiding the register, David Jones shares fell 11 cents yesterday to A$1.57 following a series of profit downgrades by stock analysts in the wake of the retailer's surprise warning last Friday of halved profits. Page 12.

Following solid exploration success in the United States, First Australian Resources shares rose 11.5 cents yesterday to finish at 36.5 cents, a result which indicates the junior has joined the growing number of Australian oil and gas companies to enjoy srong market support after expanding to the US. Page 15.

Boosted after posting a profit of A$210.9 million in its first year as a listed entity, up from A$115.5 million in the previous 12-month period, life insurance group National Mutual has predicted a strong outlook in its annual report, with earnings expectd to be achieved through increased offshore exposure and cost-cutting in the coming years. Page 15.
THE AGE

Lend Lease shares closed 10 cents higher than Friday's close yesterday as the market cautiously welcomed the group's plan to buy the largest US manager of pension fund real estate, Equitable Real Estate Investment Management, which has about A$31 billion of funds under management. Page C1.

After David Jones announced last week that its interim earnings would fall by 50 per cent to about A$22 million and its shares slumped 6.6 per cent to A$1.56 yesterday, questions are now being raised about the retailer's strategy and the timing of the Novmber 1995 float. Page C1.

St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank has hit a hurdle after the Supreme Court yesterday questioned the fairness and legality of the procedure for the deal, requesting that Advance provide written submissions on aspects of the takeover plan. The hearing was adjourned until today to give the bank time. Page C1.

Shares in Perth-based oil and gas explorer and producer First Australian Resources closed more than 44 per cent higher at 37.5 cents yesterday on the back of news of "significant" test flows from a well in Louisiana, United States. The well tested at the rate of 5.26 million cubic feet of gas and 687 barrels of oil a day. Page C1.

According to National Mutual Holdings' annual report released yesterday, managing director Geoff Tomlinson has been offered a 45 per cent pay rise to A$1,162,000 and 775,000 options in the company, subject to shareholder approval at the annual meeting next month. Page C1.

Highlands Gold shares closed at 79 cents yesterday after more than 4.48 million shares were traded in a flurry of activity that showed market approval for Highlands' proposal to sell its 25 per cent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea to Placer Dome Inc. Page C1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
